To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the S. pombe Sir2p protein functions in the establishment and maintenance of transcriptional silencing and is targeted to silent chromatin in a manner similar to its S. cerevisiae counterpart.
Sir2p functions at telomeres prior to the localization of Swip6p and that the S. cerevisiae S. cerevisia SIR2 gene functions in place of S, pombe sir2.
the Schizosacch. pombe Sir2 protein is required for transcriptional silencing at telomeres, centromeres, and silent mating-type loc.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how the SIR2 gene product is involved in the establishment of chromatin silencing in fission yeast.
the role of histone deacetylation in gene silencing in S. pombe and its relationship to other silencing mechanisms.
the molecular mechanisms of gene silencing in yeast.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Sir2p functions in the silencing of all three loci, but that the molecular mechanisms of silencing are different.
S. pombe and S. cerevisiae Sir2 proteins are conserved in their ability to deacetylate histones at silent chromatin.
Sir2p is required for the establishment of silencing at all four chromosomal regions in S. pombe, and it is required for the localization of the Swi6p protein at telomeres, but not at centromeres.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Sir2p is essential for the formation of heterochromatin, and that Sir2p and Swi6p are functionally redundant in the establishment of telomeric silencing.
the S. pombe Sir2p is required for the establishment of silencing and for the localization of the Swi6p protein at telomeres, the silent mating-type locus and possibly at centromeres.

the Sir2p deacetylation activity is required for full silencing at centromeres and telomeres, but not at the mating-type loci, in Schizosaccharamyces pombe, and that the Sir2 homologs of Saccharomyces pompe and Saccharomyces cerveisiae have similar silencing functions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Sir2p functions in S. pombe in a manner similar to that of SIR2p in S. cerevisiae.
the SIR2 genes of S. pomce and S. cerevisiae share a conserved function in chromatin silencing.
the Sir2 proteins in both S. pombe and S. cerevisiae have conserved silencing functions.
